sentences.en: Hello everybody and welcome back to the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》。

sentences.en: The podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客中，我们探讨二十岁时经历的一些重大生活变化和过渡，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，让我们一起剖析二十岁的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to look into, we're going to explore, I think one of the most important concepts when it comes to building healthy, realistic relationships in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要深入探讨我认为在二十岁建立健康、现实的人际关系时，最重要的概念之一。

sentences.en: Whether that's when we are dating, when we are building new friendships, or even as we begin to see our parents as real people and kind of navigating that new relationship.
sentences.zh: 无论是约会、建立新友谊，还是开始以成年人的视角看待父母并处理这种新关系时，都是如此。

sentences.en: What we're talking about is fantasy bonding.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈论的是“幻想联结”（fantasy bonding）。

sentences.en: Fantasy bonding is one of those concepts taken from psychology that I've definitely seen gaining a lot of popularity and colloquial usage in online spaces.
sentences.zh: 幻想联结是一个源自心理学的概念，我肯定它在网络空间中正变得越来越流行，并被广泛使用。

sentences.en: And it often is used to kind of refer to the bonds we create with potential partners or love interests in a very kind of like misconstrued sense.
sentences.zh: 它通常被用来指代我们与潜在伴侣或心仪对象之间建立的一种非常扭曲的联结。

sentences.en: Often we think that fantasy bonding is, you know, just this idea of like having a fantasy about someone and therefore bonding with them over it, which is in some ways true.
sentences.zh: 我们通常认为幻想联结就是对某人产生幻想，并因此与他们建立联结，这在某种程度上是对的。

sentences.en: But I think it ignores a lot of the really important psychological origins that are not understood.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它忽略了许多尚未被理解的、非常重要的心理起源。

sentences.en: And that is such a shame, because once we really understand the nature of fantasy bonding, I think so much about our lives begins to make so much more sense.
sentences.zh: 这真的很可惜，因为一旦我们真正理解了幻想联结的本质，我认为我们生活中的许多事情就会变得更有意义。

sentences.en: We can gain a whole new understanding of how we approach relationships, why that is.
sentences.zh: 我们可以对我们如何处理人际关系以及原因获得全新的理解。

sentences.en: And we begin to be able to identify the kind of invisible string or pattern that ties a lot of our relationships together.
sentences.zh: 我们开始能够识别出将我们许多人际关系联系在一起的那种无形的纽带或模式。

sentences.en: And that is that a lot of the time we are a lot more attached to our idea of someone or we are or their potential than the reality of who they actually are.
sentences.zh: 那就是，很多时候我们对某人的想法或他们的潜力，比对他们真实的样子要执着得多。

sentences.en: Our relationships become defined a lot more by our perceptions, by wishful thinking, sometimes even willful ignorance,
sentences.zh: 我们的人际关系更多地是由我们的感知、一厢情愿的想法，有时甚至是刻意的无知所定义的，

sentences.en: than who this person and what this relationship truly could be.
sentences.zh: 而不是由这个人真实的样子以及这段关系真正可能成为的样子所定义。

sentences.en: So let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们来谈谈它。

sentences.en: First off, I really want to start by giving you a bit of history behind where this term originated, because although it's usually used to refer to dating and instances of dating,
sentences.zh: 首先，我真的想从这个术语的起源历史讲起，因为虽然它通常被用来指代约会和约会中的情况，

sentences.en: it starts a lot earlier than that.
sentences.zh: 但它开始得要早得多。

sentences.en: So fantasy bonding was a term created by Dr. Robert Firestone in his book, literally titled The Fantasy Bomb.
sentences.zh: “幻想联结”是由罗伯特·法尔斯通博士（Dr. Robert Firestone）在他那本名为《幻想联结》（The Fantasy Bond）的书中提出的术语。

sentences.en: And it was published quite a while ago, almost 40 years ago in 1985.
sentences.zh: 它出版于很久以前，几乎是40年前的1985年。

sentences.en: And he used it to describe primarily the connection we typically form with our parents and how we all have essentially this emotional hunger
sentences.zh: 他用它来描述我们通常与父母建立的联结，以及我们所有人本质上都有这种情感饥渴，

sentences.en: and need to see our parents or our caregivers as utterly perfect and endlessly able to provide us with all of our needs, all of the love, comfort,
sentences.zh: 以及将父母或照顾者视为绝对完美、能够无止境地满足我们所有需求、提供所有爱、安慰、

sentences.en: resources that we need, but also the security that we crave.
sentences.zh: 资源的渴望，同时也渴望他们提供我们所追求的安全感。

sentences.en: Even when sometimes they aren't able to do that.
sentences.zh: 即使有时他们无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: So therefore, based on this bond, based on this fantasy that we have of our parents, we end up idealizing them in order to trust them through everything.
sentences.zh: 因此，基于这种联结，基于我们对父母的这种幻想，我们最终会理想化他们，以便在任何情况下都信任他们。

sentences.en: So essentially, a fantasy bond in this form is what we would call a primitive defense mechanism.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，这种形式的幻想联结就是我们所说的原始防御机制。

sentences.en: And we, like I said, develop it in early childhood as a way of maintaining an illusion of safety and security that is tied to our parents.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们在童年早期就发展出这种机制，作为一种维持与父母相连的安全感和保障感幻觉的方式。

sentences.en: Even when we are experiencing a lot of hurt or terror, it lets us see our parents as our savior in an attempt to kind of cope with emotional pain.
sentences.zh: 即使当我们经历很多伤害或恐惧时，它也让我们把父母视为救世主，试图以此来应对情感痛苦。

sentences.en: When we are, as children, really terrified or scared or hurt, we have this kind of vision of our parents as being able to fix that for us.
sentences.zh: 当我们还是孩子，感到非常恐惧、害怕或受伤时，我们会在脑海中构想出父母能够为我们解决这些问题。

sentences.en: We have this version of our parents in our imagination who are, and we see them as these all-powerful, all-healing, kind of god-like people.
sentences.zh: 我们在想象中拥有一个父母的版本，我们将他们视为全能、全愈、神一般的人。

sentences.en: And a lot of our relationship with them in the early years of our lives
sentences.zh: 我们在生命早期的许多与他们的关系中，

sentences.en: incorporates that fantasy bond.
sentences.zh: 都包含了这种幻想联结。

sentences.en: So if you think about it, if we were from a very young age to see our parents the way that we see them now in our 20s as kind of real humans, as flawed people as everyone is,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想一想，如果我们从很小的时候就以现在二十岁时的眼光看待父母，把他们看作像每个人一样有缺陷的真实人类，

sentences.en: if we were to see them that way as a children, that would, as children, that would have made us feel a lot less safe about the world,
sentences.zh: 如果我们作为孩子那样看待他们，那会让我们对世界感到少很多安全感，

sentences.en: especially at times when we were really vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 特别是在我们非常脆弱的时候。

sentences.en: So it's only as we get older that we really begin to realize that our parents can't stop us from feeling pain.
sentences.zh: 所以只有当我们长大后，我们才真正开始意识到父母无法阻止我们感到痛苦。

sentences.en: They can't cure all our illnesses.
sentences.zh: 他们无法治愈我们所有的疾病。

sentences.en: They can't stop terrible things from happening and that, in fact, they may, at times, be just as scared as us.
sentences.zh: 他们无法阻止可怕的事情发生，事实上，有时他们可能和我们一样害怕。

sentences.en: So this fantasy bond serves a purpose in our early childhood.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种幻想联结在我们的童年早期起到了一定的作用。

sentences.en: It also can sometimes protect us from remembering the times that our parents weren't the best parents, the times that they screwed up or they hurt us or they did the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 它有时也能保护我们，让我们不去回想父母表现不佳、搞砸了、伤害了我们或做错事的时刻。

sentences.en: Because as children, we really have no one else to rely on but these caregivers.
sentences.zh: 因为作为孩子，我们除了这些照顾者之外，真的无人可依。

sentences.en: And yet we are so fragile.
sentences.zh: 然而我们又是如此脆弱。

sentences.en: And so if there was to be something that would cause us to not see our parents as being able to help us and being these, like, very powerful creatures, we really wouldn't have
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有什么事情导致我们不再认为父母能够帮助我们，不再认为他们是那种非常强大的存在，我们真的就不会有

sentences.en: any sense of security in the world.
sentences.zh: 任何世界安全感了。

sentences.en: Most people grow out of the fantasy bond that they have with their parents.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会随着成长而摆脱与父母之间的幻想联结。

sentences.en: It becomes more realistic.
sentences.zh: 它会变得更加现实。

sentences.en: For those that don't, we have people who will continue to idealize their parents and family seeing it through rose-colored lenses.
sentences.zh: 对于那些没有摆脱的人，他们会继续理想化自己的父母和家庭，戴着玫瑰色眼镜看待一切。

sentences.en: Maybe you have encountered people who are like, oh, you know, there was always something wrong with me as a kid.
sentences.zh: 也许你遇到过这样的人，他们会说，哦，你知道，我小时候总是自己有问题。

sentences.en: My parents were great.
sentences.zh: 我的父母很棒。

sentences.en: Like, I was a bad kid.
sentences.zh: 我是一个坏孩子。

sentences.en: They did whatever they could.
sentences.zh: 他们尽了他们所能。

sentences.en: They're like my hero.
sentences.zh: 他们就像我的英雄。

sentences.en: They're amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们太棒了。

sentences.en: I think that some of those, like, appraisals are good things to have.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一些评价是好事。

sentences.en: Like, respecting your parents, loving your parents, appreciating them.
sentences.zh: 比如尊重父母、爱父母、欣赏他们。

sentences.en: Totally normal.
sentences.zh: 这完全正常。

sentences.en: And sometimes there is nothing wrong with our childhoods that would cause us to not believe that.
sentences.zh: 有时我们的童年并没有什么问题，导致我们不相信这一点。

sentences.en: But I think this more refers to people who have had this fantasy bond to the point, this fantasy bond to the point where it's kind of created an unbalanced relationship.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这更多是指那些拥有这种幻想联结，以至于造成了不平衡关系的人。

sentences.en: For example, maybe they bring a new family member in.
sentences.zh: 例如，也许他们带了一个新家庭成员进来。

sentences.en: They start dating someone.
sentences.zh: 他们开始和某人约会。

sentences.en: They've talked about how their family is, like, amazing.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论他们的家庭是多么棒。

sentences.en: Their parents could do anything.
sentences.zh: 他们的父母无所不能。

sentences.en: And then, like, the new girlfriend, the new boyfriend, the new partner comes in and is like, whoa, like, there's a lot going on here.
sentences.zh: 然后，新的女朋友、新的男朋友、新的伴侣进来了，心想，哇，这儿有很多问题啊。

sentences.en: This, my partner is definitely, like, has this idea of their parents that is not real.
sentences.zh: 我的伴侣绝对是对他们的父母有一种不切实际的想法。

sentences.en: The other thing that a fantasy bond does is that once we have kind of learnt that we can dissociate from the reality of who someone is and create a version of them
sentences.zh: 幻想联结的另一件事是，一旦我们学会了可以脱离某人的真实情况，并创造出一个

sentences.en: that is useful for us, we can begin to replicate that bond in our adult relationships,
sentences.zh: 对我们有用的版本，我们就可以开始在成年后的关系中复制这种联结，

sentences.en: primarily in our romantic lives.
sentences.zh: 主要是在我们的浪漫生活中。

sentences.en: And that is what I really want to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 而这正是今天我真正想谈论的。

sentences.en: This is when we get the fantasy bond that we most often talk about when it comes to dating.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在约会时最常谈论的幻想联结。

sentences.en: A fantasy bond situation can be something that any of us finds ourselves in because it is basically, like, relying on a very human trait, which is our imagination.
sentences.zh: 幻想联结的情况可能是我们任何人都会发现自己陷入的，因为它基本上是依赖于一种非常人类的特质，即我们的想象力。

sentences.en: And what it does is it describes an illusion of connection between two people that is based on an idea of the love or the connection that you share rather than the truth.
sentences.zh: 它描述的是两个人之间的一种联结幻觉，这种联结是基于你所分享的爱或联结的某种想法，而不是事实。

sentences.en: It is essentially a partial delusion.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一种部分妄想。

sentences.en: It can be based on someone's potential.
sentences.zh: 它可以基于某人的潜力。

sentences.en: A potential that they might not be ready or are incapable of fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 一种他们可能还没准备好或无法实现的潜力。

sentences.en: But you hold on to the possibility because of what it could mean for you if they were to change.
sentences.zh: 但你坚持这种可能性，因为如果他们改变了，这对你意味着什么。

sentences.en: If they could be the fantasy.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能成为那个幻想中的人。

sentences.en: Essentially, it's having one version of this person in your mind and this other version of them that is real not aligning.
sentences.zh: 本质上，就是你脑海中这个人的版本与现实中他们的版本不一致。

sentences.en: But we're unable to see that gap, that conflict between the fantasy and the reality.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法看到那种差距，那种幻想与现实之间的冲突。

sentences.en: We all want to feel close to someone.
sentences.zh: 我们都想感到与某人亲近。

sentences.en: We want intimacy.
sentences.zh: 我们想要亲密感。

sentences.en: We want security.
sentences.zh: 我们想要安全感。

sentences.en: We want love.
sentences.zh: 我们想要爱。

sentences.en: We want a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一段关系。

sentences.en: And sometimes that can cause us to ignore a lack of genuine interest or compatibility or signs that this person is actually not right for us.
sentences.zh: 有时这会导致我们忽视缺乏真正的兴趣或兼容性，或者忽视这个人其实并不适合我们的迹象。

sentences.en: They actually don't give us what we need.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上并没有给我们所需要的。

sentences.en: But by indulging in the fantasy of who this is that we have created for ourselves, the relationship can still be sustained and provide us things that we want in other areas.
sentences.zh: 但通过沉溺于我们为自己创造的关于这个人的幻想，这段关系仍然可以维持，并在其他方面提供我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: Another reason this might develop is when we place unrealistic expectations on someone and we imagine that they can somehow solve all our probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这种联结发展的另一个原因是，当我们对某人抱有不切实际的期望，并想象他们能以某种方式解决我们所有问题时。

sentences.en: They are the one who can make us feel loved and chosen and seen and complete.
sentences.zh: 他们是那个能让我们感到被爱、被选择、被看见和完整的人。

sentences.en: And what this tends to do is cause us to accelerate our emotional bond.
sentences.zh: 而这往往会导致我们加速情感联结。

sentences.en: I think that love, what I've learned about love is that it should feel really natural and easy and like a gradual progression and increasing closeness.
sentences.zh: 我认为爱，我所了解的爱，应该是感觉非常自然、轻松，像是一种渐进的过程和亲密感的增加。

sentences.en: The relationships where you like meet someone and you're instantly like that is my soulmate.
sentences.zh: 那些你遇到某人，立刻觉得“那就是我的灵魂伴侣”的关系，

sentences.en: I need to tell them everything about me.
sentences.zh: 我需要告诉他们关于我的一切。

sentences.en: I've often found that, you know, it's the saying, right?
sentences.zh: 我经常发现，你知道，有句老话，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the candle that burns the brightest like goes out the fasteSt.
sentences.zh: 就像燃烧得最亮的蜡烛熄灭得最快。

sentences.en: Maybe that's this.
sentences.zh: 也许就是这样。

sentences.en: It could be something else.
sentences.zh: 也可能是别的原因。

sentences.en: But the idea is the same, right?
sentences.zh: 但道理是一样的，对吧？

sentences.en: That intensity is not sustainable.
sentences.zh: 那种强度是不可持续的。

sentences.en: And so when we find ourselves creating a fantasy bond, we are that intensity is really defining of those situations.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们发现自己创造了一个幻想联结时，那种强度确实定义了这些情况。

sentences.en: And we often force a lot of artificial intimacy with them.
sentences.zh: 我们经常强行制造很多虚假的亲密感。

sentences.en: So we might be like,
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会说，

sentences.en: I know I've only known you for a week, but let's go on a trip together.
sentences.zh: 我知道我只认识你一周，但我们一起去旅行吧。

sentences.en: Like, do you want to do you want to come on a trip?
sentences.zh: 你想去旅行吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to like go on an overseas like holiday?
sentences.zh: 你想去海外度假吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to go on a weekend away?
sentences.zh: 你想去过个周末吗？

sentences.en: Or we'll be like, oh, by the way, like my mom's in town.
sentences.zh: 或者我们会说，哦，顺便说一下，我妈妈在城里。

sentences.en: Why don't you just meet her?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不见见她？

sentences.en: Why don't you just move in?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不搬进来住？

sentences.en: You know, we've only known each other for like three weeks.
